options.void_lod.title: VOID LOD
options.void_lod.preset.tooltip: Sets reach, detail, worker threads and GPU memory together. Low suits integrated graphics, Medium a laptop GPU, High a desktop GPU, Ultra a strong one.
options.void_lod.enabled.tooltip: Draws the land past your render distance, out to the horizon. F8 turns it on and off in game.
options.void_lod.autoTune.tooltip: Coarsens the detail (and, only if that is not enough, the reach) while far terrain costs more than about 1.5 ms of GPU or 0.5 ms of CPU a frame, and restores it when there is room. Leaves the game alone while it holds its frame cap.
options.void_lod.radius.tooltip: How far the far terrain reaches. Each doubling costs one more coarse level: more memory and build time, little frame time.
options.void_lod.haze.tooltip: How far the air carries at sea level before distant land fades into the sky. Auto is three quarters of the reach.
options.void_lod.detail.tooltip: How many pixels a far terrain cell may cover on screen before it is split into finer ones. Fewer pixels is sharper and costs more: the cell count goes with the square.
options.void_lod.threads.tooltip: Threads that build far terrain in the background, at low priority. More fills in new views faster.
options.void_lod.budget.tooltip: How much video memory far terrain may hold before the least recently seen tiles are dropped.
options.void_lod.status: %s tiles, %s quads · GPU %s ms · CPU %s ms
options.void_lod.status.none: Nothing to draw here: far terrain needs a singleplayer or LAN-hosted world with open sky
